# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

This is a small Next.js site (App Router). I read all five pages, the shared layout, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `geo.config.json`. The basics are mostly in place. Four things cost points: `<html>` has no language, `robots.txt` doesn't point to the sitemap, `/pricing` is marked noindex, and `/blog` loads its content only in the browser. Nothing is unknown. I assumed you want AI search tools to find the site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a language to the `<html>` tag
- **Why it matters:** Without `lang`, search engines and assistive tools have to guess the page language.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80. Change it to `<html lang="en">`, matching `site.language` in your config.

### 2. Point `robots.txt` to your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** The sitemap exists but nothing tells crawlers where it is.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2`
- **What the code says:** `Allow: /` (the file has no `Sitemap:` line)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 = 80. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.

### 3. Decide whether `/pricing` should be indexable
- **Why it matters:** The page is in your navigation and sitemap, but it tells search engines not to index it. Its canonical (the page's preferred address) also points at a noindex URL.
- **Where:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** If the page should be found, remove that `robots` setting. That gives 18.25 ÷ 23 = 79. If the noindex is deliberate, drop it from the sitemap and the navigation instead. The score stays at 72.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt` |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | `*` allowed; only GPTBot (training) blocked, which matches your policy |
| GEO-014 | Pages are indexable | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`; 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | `/pricing` canonical points at a noindex page; `/` clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have no canonical |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8`; 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is discoverable | Problem | Sitemap exists but `robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, `lang` | Problem | `app/layout.tsx:11`, no `lang` on any route |
| GEO-016 | Key pages linked with real links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13` |
| GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Only a scoped `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:15`), which is fine |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Layout and 5 pages read; no images or buttons |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not an app project |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present; not scored |

For GEO-003, the code at `app/blog/page.tsx:8` is `fetch('/api/posts')` inside `useEffect`, so the post list isn't in the served HTML.

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:4`: `<loc>https://www.ledger.example/pricing</loc>`. The page is noindex, so the two signals contradict each other. Fix it by following item 3.
- **`/blog` can't set its own title or description:** `app/blog/page.tsx:1`: `'use client';`. Client components can't export `metadata`, so the blog shows the site-wide default title and description. Split the page into a server component that holds the metadata and a client child.

## Worth considering

- **Give blog posts their own pages:** `app/blog/page.tsx:10`: `<article key={p.id}>{p.title}</article>`. Posts show only a title and have no address. Add `/blog/[slug]` pages, link to them from the list, and add them to the sitemap.
- **Show the pricing details as text:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `Free for up to three people.` The description promises "Plans for every team size", but the page lists no plans. Add the paid tiers and their prices as text.
- **Say more on the Docs page:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` Docs is one line. Add the setup steps, and link onward to Pricing and the Blog.
- **Add canonicals to `/docs` and `/blog`:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` sets no `alternates`. The layout already has `metadataBase`, so a canonical of `/docs` would resolve correctly. Better still, set a default in the layout.
- **Mark up the organisation:** `app/layout.tsx:3`: `title: 'Ledger: accounting for small teams'`. No Organization or WebSite JSON-LD states the name and site address in machine-readable form. This could help tools identify the site.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3` has no dates. Real dates could help crawlers know what changed. Consider generating the sitemap from `app/sitemap.ts` instead of keeping it by hand.
- **Make the home page say more:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` Each of those could link to a page with detail.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** real status codes, redirects and `X-Robots-Tag` headers, and whether the sitemap URLs answer 200. A live scan would confirm these.
- **`/api/posts`:** there is no route file in the repo, so I can't tell where the blog data comes from.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which matches your config.
- `/thank-you` is deliberately noindex and kept out of the sitemap and navigation, so I left it out of the route counts.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
